summary: Job closeout verification. Cleanup verified via Postgres, read only: jobs=837, 0 jobs with scheduled_end<scheduled_start, INV-0029 gone, purchase_orders=2248, inventory_txns 1561 / sum(delta) 13131.5, sum(materials.quantity_on_hand) 16031.5, users = exactly the 4 kept accounts. No orphan rows found in purchase_orders, job_materials, job_cost_snapshots, actual_cost_entries, inventory_txns or invoices. 11 TEST_P4_Lead jobs with valid dates remain, as intended. New backend suite tests/test_iter131_closeout.py: 14/14 passed. It covers the assignable type-ahead (search by name/email ignoring case, active users only, deactivated user never returned, no-q lists all active users, limit works, sales 403, office allowed), assigning an inactive or unknown user (422 on office and mobile assign), the sales PO list/detail/status-history (own job only, total and unit_cost/line_total/abc_price null, other PO 404), Job Detail purchase_orders (no total key for sales, total for owner), another sales user 403/404, and Crew A jobs (mobile shows assigned_to, crew_id and crew_name). Regression: test_assignments, test_job_crews_readiness_iter129, test_iter130_retest and phase4 test_job_schedule_repeat_no_error gave 21 passed, 2 failed, 6 errors. Every failure and error is caused by the deleted JOB-0257 (an end<start test job) still being hardcoded in iter129/iter130 tests, not by an app bug. Quote accept making the rep the Job Manager (and another sales user getting 403), crew assignment and install-date validation all passed. Test cleanup works: after both runs the users count was back to 4 (the hook printed 'removed 3 automated-test user(s)'). Frontend (Playwright, desktop): as owner, the Job Manager picker searches through the server (debounced /users/assignable?q=...&limit=25 calls), shows the empty state, saves a pick with the toast 'Job manager: Sales Backup Test', and updates job-fact-manager and the trigger. Unassigning with job-manager-picker-none shows 'Job manager cleared'. The crew select still works. Owner sees job-po-total and the PO card opens /purchase-orders/:id. As sales_bk on that job: status badge and supplier (job-po-meta) shown, no job-po-total, card does nothing when clicked, read-only manager/crew, no Costing section, and /purchase-orders/:id redirects to /. The test job (JOB-0692) was assigned to sales_bk and then put back to unassigned.

minor.issue: LIKE wildcards are not escaped: q='%' or '_' matches every user (q=% returned all 6). It can't leak anything because results are still active-only and manage-only, but searching a literal underscore (e.g. 'sales_') matches too broadly. Escape % _ \ and use .like(..., escape='\\').

Unlike mobile job assign, the mobile lead assign does not check that the user exists and is active, and uuid.UUID() on bad input gives a 500. Not in this scope, but it doesn't match the 'validate assignee' rule.

ui_bugs.issue: No guard against out-of-order responses. Overlapping requests (typing slower than the 200ms debounce on a slow network) can show results for an older query. Ignore stale responses with a request counter or AbortController.

action_items: Update tests/test_job_crews_readiness_iter129.py (test_job_0257_materials_short, test_legacy_inverted_status_only_ok) and tests/test_iter130_retest.py (jobs_pair fixture) to stop using the deleted JOB_0257 (3f92f045-...). Pick a job dynamically or build one in setup.

Existing regression tests (test_assignments.py, iter129 quote-accept, phase4) create leads/quotes/customers/jobs and never delete them. Only users and price books are purged at session end, so jobs still pile up; this run created 3 and I deleted them by id. Add teardown, or extend the session cleanup to these records using the strict test pattern.
Optional: escape LIKE wildcards in list_assignable; add a stale-response guard in UserSearchPicker.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/purchasing.py: sales cost redaction is applied after building the response in list_pos, get_po and status_history, and _sales_po_guard returns 404 for POs not on the user's jobs. Correct. status_history has no cost fields.
routers/jobs.py get_job: the total key is left out for sales; purchase_orders is an untyped list in JobDetailOut, so the key really is absent (verified).
routers/users.py list_assignable: filters is_active and role in ROLES; q is length-capped at 100 and limit must be 1-100. Wildcards are not escaped (minor).

tests/_test_data_cleanup.py: TEST_USER_RE plus KEEP_USERS protects the kept accounts; the owner's domain doesn't match. Note the last branch '[a-z]+_test|test_[a-z0-9_]+' + hex@example.com is broad, but it only acts on users created after the session snapshot (only_new_since), so pre-existing users are safe.
